title: How do we fill the grid so it has exactly two fold lines?
description: An eight by eight grid of square tiles has its top left quarter filled, and two red lines cross at the middle. Taking the mirror picture of the filled quarter across the red lines fills the other three quarters, and then each red line is checked by folding. Keeko raises the doubt that the quarter can be copied without flipping it.
teaching_notes: One idea: to make a red line a line of symmetry, fill the other side with the mirror picture of the filled side, flipped over that line. Watch for students who copy the filled quarter without flipping it, so the slanting lines lean the wrong way.

source: Use the colour tiles given at the end of the book to complet
video_script.why: The child learns to build a figure with chosen lines of symmetry by taking the mirror picture of a filled part across each line.
video_script.substitution: The book's own grid of coloured tiles, with the top left quarter filled and the two red lines through the middle.
video_script.anchor: the book's eight by eight grid of square tiles, each cut by a slanting line into a blue triangle and a yellow triangle, with the top left quarter filled and a red vertical line and a red horizontal line through the middle
video_script.wrong_answer: copy the filled quarter without flipping it
video_script.wrong_move: copies the filled quarter into the other quarters without flipping it, so the slanting lines lean the wrong way when the grid is folded on a red line
video_script.payoff_line: The other three quarters are mirror pictures of the filled quarter

final_answer.value: the other three quarters are mirror images of the filled quarter; exactly 2 lines of symmetry, the two red lines
final_answer.spoken: the other three quarters are mirror pictures of the filled quarter, and the figure has exactly two lines of symmetry, the two red lines

hold_back: mirror images of the filled quarter
never_show: a quarter copied without flipping it shown as correct
a figure with slanting fold lines drawn as lines of symmetry
maths_rules: the grid is 8 tiles by 8 tiles, so each quarter is 4 tiles by 4 tiles
the top left quarter is filled; the red vertical line and the red horizontal line cross at the middle
step 1: the top right quarter is the mirror picture of the top left quarter across the red vertical line; each tile flips, so its slanting line leans the other way
step 2: the bottom half is the mirror picture of the top half across the red horizontal line
check: the grid folds on the red vertical line and the red horizontal line and the halves match, so these are 2 lines of symmetry
check: the slanting folds from corner to corner do not match for the book's figure, so there are exactly 2 lines
slip: an unflipped copy of the quarter does not match when the grid is folded on the red line
video_script.design: One idea: the mirror picture across a line makes that line a line of symmetry. One grid all video, blue and yellow triangles for the tiles, red for the two middle lines, teal for the flip arrows.
